clue.text: With eleven in the box, is one intent on defence?

definitions.text: With eleven in the box, is one intent on defence?

blocks.note: reads as a football team crowding its penalty box; really the other eleven members of a jury seated in the jury box
reads as a defender; really someone listening intently to the case the defence puts

explanation.surface: A football defender, one of eleven, guarding the penalty box.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleven and the box suggest a football team and its penalty area, but a juror sits in the jury box with eleven others, listening intently to the case for the defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury has twelve members, so each juror sits in the box with eleven others and must hear the defence out.

clue.text: Daughter in prison treated by psychiatrist quick to offer opinion

blocks.note: jug is slang for prison
D = daughter, placed inside JUG to make JUDG
a mental patient is one a psychiatrist treats

explanation.surface: A daughter behind bars is seen by the prison psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: JUDGMENTAL without the E after G is a standard spelling, so the letters fit exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone judgmental is quick to pass opinions on others.

clue.text: Latin matters for language students taking their finals

indicators.note: a word's final is its last letter, so take the last letter of each word

blocks.note: the last letters of foR, languagE and studentS

explanation.surface: Latin is a subject for language students sitting their final exams.
explanation.walkthrough: Finals looks like exams; here it means the final letters of the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: RES is the Latin for things or matters, as in 'res judicata'.

clue.text: Eg split trousers in use again for the present

indicators.note: as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so the split holds EG inside it

blocks.note: a rift is a split
the word itself, taken whole and placed after the first letter of the split

explanation.surface: Someone has split their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Trousers is a verb here, meaning pockets or holds. The definition is a pun: a present is a gift, not the current moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To regift is to pass on a present you were given, using it again as a present.

clue.text: Fraud cases from Iraqi city disturbed trustee

indicators.note: a word's case is its outside, so take the outer letters
the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken whole
the outer letters of IraqI and CitY

explanation.surface: A fraud trial in which the cases come from an Iraqi city.
explanation.walkthrough: Iraqi city tempts you to look for UR or BASRA; it only supplies its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiduciary holds property or power in trust for another, which is what a trustee does.

clue.text: Blonde’s good-looking? Only just, I suppose

blocks.note: fair-haired means blonde
the 's is short for is
fair is an old word for beautiful

explanation.surface: Is the blonde good-looking? Only just, you would grudgingly say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only just' reads as barely, as if damning the blonde's looks; in the definition it means only fair, just being a synonym of fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying fair's fair concedes that something is only just, as in right and even-handed.

clue.text: Strict rules make old lady bored by golf

definitions.note: DOGMA is a singular noun for a body of fixed rules or beliefs.

blocks.note: to do is to make, as in do a sketch
G = golf in the phonetic alphabet
old lady is slang for mother, MA

explanation.surface: An old lady is bored stiff by a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: Bored reads as uninterested, which suits the golf; here it means drilled into, the passive making golf the drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down as beyond question.

clue.text: Your flipping dog is on top of mine

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over
in a down clue the dog sits above the rest

blocks.note: a collie is a sheepdog
yr is the written abbreviation of your, flipped to RY

explanation.surface: Someone swears that your dog is sitting on top of theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: Mine reads as the possessive; it is the definition, a coal mine. 'Flipping' also works as a mild British curse in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal mine together with its buildings.

clue.text: Nail net up at ground before match

indicators.note: the letters are ground up and remade

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: A groundsman fixes the goal net in place at the ground before kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground and match point to football; the match is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenuptial means before a wedding, as in an antenuptial contract.

clue.text: Casual greeting from slangy youngsters

blocks.note: yo is a slang hello
of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'

explanation.surface: Young people greet each other casually in slang.
explanation.walkthrough: YOOF is British slang, a jokey spelling of youth for young people as a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoof is a slang word for young people, so it is youngsters put slangily.

clue.text: Tricky writing name on second pair of underpants

indicators.note: take the second pair of letters in the word, its third and fourth

blocks.note: unDErpants: letters three and four
signing is writing your name

explanation.surface: Someone writes their name in their second pair of underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the signing after DE across the grid. Second pair of underpants sounds like spare laundry but points at letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A designing person is scheming and crafty, which is tricky.

clue.text: Pound to put each way, small stakes gambling

indicators.note: TO is written both backwards and forwards: OT then TO

blocks.note: L = pound, from the Latin libra
TO backwards then forwards

explanation.surface: A punter puts a pound each way on a horse, a small-stakes bet.
explanation.walkthrough: Each way is betting slang for a win-or-place bet; here it means the word read in each direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery, a form of gambling where a small stake is paid for a ticket.

clue.text: Evidence soldier provided first in establishing rank

indicators.note: take the first letter in the word that follows

blocks.note: a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men
if = provided that
the first letter of Establishing
station means rank or standing, as in above your station

explanation.surface: A soldier supplies evidence to establish his rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Rank reads as military grade to match the soldier; STATION is social standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifestation is a sign that shows something exists, which is evidence of it.

clue.text: Sir’s unenthusiastic by the sound of it, teaching after hours

indicators.note: the words are said out loud and heard as other words

blocks.note: a knight is addressed as Sir, and cool means unenthusiastic

explanation.surface: The teacher, called Sir, sounds reluctant about teaching extra hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir looks like a schoolteacher, fitting the surface; it stands for a knight, who is styled Sir.
explanation.definitionFit: Night school holds classes in the evening, after normal working hours.

clue.text: Relief because case isn’t complicated

indicators.note: the letters are tangled into a new order

blocks.note: as = because, as in 'as it was raining'
anagram of CASE ISNT, dropping the apostrophe

explanation.surface: It is a relief that a legal case turns out to be simple.
explanation.walkthrough: Relief means aid here, as in famine relief, not the feeling of ease the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the charitable sense: famine relief is help sent to those in need.

clue.text: When cycling, bump in the road is always annoying

indicators.note: a cycle goes round and round, so the first letter travels round to the end

blocks.note: a snag is a small obstacle or hitch

explanation.surface: A cyclist finds every bump in the road irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling reads as riding a bike, which the bump in the road supports; it means SNAG's S moves round to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who nags keeps on annoying you with complaints.

clue.text: Unsuitable rooms appal cooks

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or rework, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: Cooks are horrified by the unsuitable kitchens they must work in.
explanation.walkthrough: Cooks looks like the subject of appal; it is a verb acting on the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Malapropos means inappropriate or out of place, so unsuitable.

clue.text: All good parts celebrated in later life

blocks.note: great = celebrated, famous
G = good, split into GREAT as GRE-G-AT
age = old age, later life; the rest goes in after its second letter

explanation.surface: A cheerful claim that the whole of old age is good.
explanation.walkthrough: Parts reads as a noun, portions of life; it is a verb, the letter splitting the word it enters, and the result is then boxed in.
explanation.definitionFit: The aggregate is the total, everything taken together.

clue.text: Model or muse of the Beatles, say

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: A model who was muse to the Beatles, such as Pattie Boyd.
explanation.walkthrough: Model reads as a person, a pairing with muse; it is a verb acting on the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles were four musicians, a foursome; 'say' marks them as an example.

clue.text: Last bits of malt whisky in a bottle show maturity

indicators.note: take the last letter of each word

blocks.note: the word itself
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
malT and whiskY, placed after the first letter of the courage

explanation.surface: The dregs of a single malt left in the bottle show it has aged well.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle and whisky belong together in the surface, but bottle is the slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom, usually a rebuke to someone behaving childishly, telling them to behave like the grown-up they are.

clue.text: Very short motorway towards the centre is unfinished

indicators.note: the last letter of IS is dropped

blocks.note: M = motorway, as on British road signs
in = inwards, towards the centre
IS without its last letter

explanation.surface: A short stretch of motorway to the city centre has not been finished.
explanation.walkthrough: British motorways are numbered with an M prefix, as in the M1, so M alone stands for motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini means very small or short, as in a miniskirt.

clue.text: Hammer essential for building work

blocks.note: walls are essential to a building
op = opus, a work

explanation.surface: A hammer is an essential tool for building work.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammer is a verb, not the tool the surface shows, and WALL comes from a loose description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both mean to strike hard and repeatedly, or to beat an opponent heavily.

clue.text: Later note debutante wearing pink give thumbs up to ensemble

blocks.note: coral is a pinkish colour; it goes round PS DEB
a PS, postscript, is a note added later
deb is the clipped short form of debutante, its first three letters
to let is to allow, give the thumbs up

explanation.surface: A debutante in pink gets approval, noted later in the society pages.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante is a young upper-class woman launched into society; DEB is her usual short form.
explanation.definitionFit: The corps de ballet is the ensemble of dancers who perform together behind the soloists.

clue.text: Seeing that act described in confession drained constable

indicators.note: the inside is emptied out, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: confession is where a sin is described
ConstablE with its middle emptied

explanation.surface: A policeman is worn out after describing an act in his statement.
explanation.walkthrough: The confession sounds like one to the police, which the constable supports; it is a religious one.
explanation.definitionFit: Since can mean seeing that, as in 'since you ask'.

clue.text: Member left half of drink

indicators.note: keep only the first half of the word

blocks.note: L = left
IMBibe cut in half; to imbibe is to drink

explanation.surface: A club member has left half a drink on the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Drink is a verb, IMBIBE, and only half of it is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a member of the body, an arm or leg.

clue.text: Tree golf club lopped fell during round

indicators.note: the end of the word is cut off, as a branch is lopped

blocks.note: IRON with its last letter cut off
a knockout, KO, fells a boxer during a round

explanation.surface: A golfer fells a tree with a club during a round.
explanation.walkthrough: Fell looks like a tree-felling verb or the past of fall; it is a boxer's knockdown. IROKO is a West African hardwood.
explanation.definitionFit: The iroko is a large tropical African tree valued for its timber.

clue.text: Spooner’s only granny who didn’t quite make it?

definitions.note: The definition is a relative clause, standing for one who didn't quite make it.

indicators.note: Rev Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: merely = only; its opening M swaps with the N of the next word
nan is British for granny; its opening N swaps with the M before it

explanation.surface: An only granny wonders about the one who didn't quite make it.
explanation.walkthrough: A nearly man is British slang for someone who keeps coming close to success without achieving it.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom, often used of sportsmen and politicians who keep finishing runner-up; the question mark flags the definition as descriptive.

clue.text: Stop running around in a frenzy

indicators.note: the word is turned around

blocks.note: to dam is to stop a flow of water

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop running around in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: Running around sounds like the frenzy itself; it turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of wildly excited, as in a mad rush, not the clinical sense.

clue.text: Nothing yielded by inamorata before viewing room

indicators.note: the O is given up by BELOVED

blocks.note: BELOVED, an inamorata, gives up its O (nothing)
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A lover yields nothing before showing a room.
explanation.walkthrough: An inamorata is a female lover, the beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a room or gallery built to command a fine view.

clue.text: Pop-up ad revolted housing minister

indicators.note: the words house the answer inside them

blocks.note: sitting in uP AD REvolted

explanation.surface: A pop-up ad disgusted a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Minister reads as a politician, and the housing minister is a real job; the minister is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain, a minister of religion, especially in the forces.
